attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: Yang-Mills analysis has not supplied a uniform reflected Wilson boundary OPE giving H,K and the o(eps^2) remainder for coincident hairpin footprints.
steps: Use fixed-collar RG convergence to pass regulated reflection positivity to a collar-limit matrix N_delta>=0 for the locked Wilson block.
Separate harmless diagonal Wilson normalizations and multiplicative boundary Gram factors; after normalization the intended same-theory block is q_delta=Nhat_delta oslash Bhat_delta.
Decompose C^n=Ce oplus 1^perp. The Schur complement of the Ce block gives eps PHP + eps^2(PKP-n^{-1}PHee^*HP)+o(eps^2).
PSD of q_delta forces PHP>=0; if PHP has null vectors, the eps^2 Schur-complement form must be nonnegative on ker(PHP).
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite-matrix implication is valid, but it only tests realized quotient blocks once the analytic collar expansion and same-theory factorization are proved.

assumptions: A fixed finite Wilson family has normalized quotient q_delta with Hermitian uniform expansion through order eps^2, eps=delta^alpha.
Additive boundary contacts vanish after diagonal trace continuity; remaining anomaly is multiplicative with nonzero entries.
P is the orthogonal projection onto 1^perp and e=n^{-1/2}1; q_delta is the realized target block, not an arbitrary Schur multiplier cone.
definitions: source object: finite reflected Wilson collar OS matrices N_delta with cutoff limits already valid by closed-cone positivity.
target object: normalized same-theory OS block q_delta whose PSD property is the continuum OS positivity test for the locked Wilson observables.
controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions through finite reflected quadratic forms and collar collapse.
same-theory condition: boundary factors may be removed only by diagonal congruence already present in the locked Wilson normalization; no boundary algebra or counterterm is added.

equations.label: normalized quotient expansion
equations.valid_when: The boundary Wilson OPE is uniform for the finite reflected collar block and all normalized entries are defined.

equations.label: first tangent gate
equations.valid_when: The expansion above is valid and the rank-one term 11^* is the vacuum OS direction.

equations.label: second tangent gate
equations.valid_when: q_delta is PSD for small delta; this is the Schur complement of the large rank-one direction.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A single z in 1^perp with z^*PHPz<0, or z in ker(PHP) with negative corrected K-form, is a finite Wilson falsifier of the same-theory bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Bridge lemma reducing Wilson collar OS preservation to computable boundary OPE coefficients H,K with a normalization-safe Schur correction.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a locked finite Wilson collar block, same-theory OS positivity after boundary-factor removal is governed near the rank-one vacuum matrix by PHP on 1^perp and, on its null space, by the Schur-corrected second boundary OPE coefficient.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if Wilson boundary OPE lacks uniform second-order expansion or forces a boundary counterterm to define q_delta.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a dense locked Wilson core has uniform H,K expansions with PHP>=0 and corrected K nonnegative, plus fixed-collar OS convergence.
control_decision.reason: The branch now has a concrete finite-matrix lemma and an analytic target: compute H,K for reflected Wilson hairpins instead of renaming the topology.

dependency_updates.description: Fixed-collar closed-cone positivity is retained; the nonformal step is now the Wilson boundary quotient tangent test.
The locked Wilson core must realize q_delta directly; diagonal congruences are allowed, boundary algebra changes are not.
Topology must control finite reflected Wilson OPE coefficients H,K with uniform second-order collar remainders.

falsifiers: First-order falsifier: compute a reflected Wilson hairpin block with z^*PHPz<0 for some z in 1^perp.
Second-order falsifier: PHP>=0 but z^*(PKP-n^{-1}PHee^*HP)z<0 on ker(PHP).
Expansion falsifier: cusp logarithms or perimeter terms make the remainder nonuniform, so the tangent test is not valid for cutoff removal.
Same-theory falsifier: collar collapse needs a boundary counterterm or enlarged Wilson algebra before q_delta becomes PSD.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 225 converts the Wilson obstruction into a valid normalization-safe tangent-cone bridge. The rank-one OS vacuum direction forces the correction -n^{-1}PHee^*HP, so PKP alone is not the right test. Pure one-body renormalizations cancel; a negative corrected form is a genuine mixed boundary falsifier.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the boundary OPE for a three- or four-hairpin reflected Wilson block, extract H,K, and test PHP and the Schur-corrected K-form on 1^perp.

cycle_learning: This research cycle converted active route pressure into typed branch lemmas. The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
